q: מטופל עם דמנציה קלה מסוגל להבין הסבר ולהחליט על ניתוח. לפי חוק זכויות החולה, כיצד יש למסור לו את המידע לצורך הסכמה מדעת?
o: במועד החתימה, בנוסח אחיד של טופס ההסכמה
לאחר קביעת הניתוח, באמצעות הודעה למשפחה
ביום הניתוח, כרשימה של יתרונות הטיפול
מוקדם ככל האפשר, בצורה מובנת לבחירה
explanation:
**יש למסור את המידע מוקדם ככל האפשר ובאופן המאפשר הבנה ובחירה חופשית.** מתאימים את ההסבר לקושי הקוגניטיבי ונותנים זמן לשאלות.

**א. טופס אחיד ברגע החתימה.** חתימה אינה מחליפה שיחה והזדמנות לשקול.
**ב. הודעה למשפחה.** המטופל עצמו מסוגל להחליט וזכאי למידע.
**ג. רק יתרונות ביום הניתוח.** נדרשים גם סיכונים, חלופות והאפשרות להימנע מטיפול.
**ד. מסירה מוקדמת ומובנת.** כך אפשר לבדוק הבנה ולקבל החלטה בלי לחץ מיותר.

אסמכתא · חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13.

q: A 72-year-old woman asks whether dietary restriction has been shown to prolong human life, as it has in some animal studies. How does Hazzard describe the human evidence?
o: Evidence of longer life without improvement in lipids or blood pressure
Evidence of improved cardiovascular measures without demonstrated longer life
Evidence of shorter life despite improvement in lipids and blood pressure
Evidence of longer life through an established biological mechanism in humans
explanation:
Dietary restriction reduces food intake while maintaining adequate nutrition. A change in blood pressure or blood lipids can be measured well before a study can tell whether people live longer.

**Human studies show improved cardiovascular measures, including blood pressure and lipid profile. A longer human lifespan has yet to be demonstrated.**

**A. Longer life without cardiovascular improvement.** Blood pressure and lipids did improve. Human survival is the outcome that remains uncertain.
**B. Improved cardiovascular measures with uncertain longevity.** These are measurable risk factors. Knowing that they improved does not tell the woman how many years the diet might add.
**C. Shorter life despite improved risk factors.** The cardiovascular findings are consistent with the studies, but the human observations also give no basis for concluding that life is shortened.
**D. Longer life through a proven mechanism.** The mechanism behind lifespan extension in animal experiments is still under investigation. Those experiments cannot show that the same intervention prolongs human life.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 6.
ref: Hazzard Ch 1 — BIOLOGY OF AGING AND LONGEVITY

optionRationales.body: . Longer life without cardiovascular improvement.** Blood pressure and lipids did improve. Human survival is the outcome that remains uncertain.
. Improved cardiovascular measures with uncertain longevity.** These are measurable risk factors. Knowing that they improved does not tell the woman how many years the diet might add.
. Shorter life despite improved risk factors.** The cardiovascular findings are consistent with the studies, but the human observations also give no basis for concluding that life is shortened.

. Longer life through a proven mechanism.** The mechanism behind lifespan extension in animal experiments is still under investigation. Those experiments cannot show that the same intervention prolongs human life.

explanationParts.text:
Dietary restriction reduces food intake while maintaining adequate nutrition. A change in blood pressure or blood lipids can be measured well before a study can tell whether people live longer.

**Human studies show improved cardiovascular measures, including blood pressure and lipid profile. A longer human lifespan has yet to be demonstrated.**
Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 6.

q: A 76-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. She has lost 6 kg in two months because of dysphagia. A video swallow study shows aspiration of thin liquids but safe swallowing of nectar-thick liquids. Her family requests a feeding tube. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, pramipexole, and quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime; MoCA during admission is 18/30. Which principle supports considering speech-therapy-guided, supervised thickened liquids?
o: Feeding tubes improve pressure-ulcer healing and should guide the choice of feeding route.
Thickened liquids are an effective compensatory option in patients with Parkinson disease.
Nasogastric tubes reduce agitation and should guide the choice of feeding route.
Swallow-study findings take priority over autonomy and quality of life in choosing the route.
explanation:
Increasing a liquid’s viscosity slows its flow and may give the patient time to protect the airway. **She could swallow the tested nectar-thick liquid safely, so a supervised oral trial with the swallowing team is reasonable.** Reassess actual fluid and calorie intake, acceptability and her preferences as delirium improves.

**A. Choose a tube for pressure-ulcer healing** — Improved healing is not an established benefit. Evidence linking tube feeding with worse pressure-injury outcomes comes chiefly from advanced dementia and cannot justify placing a tube in this woman with Parkinson disease.
**B. Try supervised thickened liquids** — A consistency that worked during this patient’s assessment is a practical compensatory option. The team should check that she tolerates and consumes enough of it.
**C. Choose a nasogastric tube for agitation** — A nasal tube may irritate or distress a delirious patient and provoke pulling at it.
**D. Let the test determine the feeding route** — Imaging informs the discussion of safety. The patient’s wishes, nutritional needs and quality of life also shape the decision.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 449–451, diet modification and oral versus nonoral intake.

q: A 75-year-old woman with Sjögren syndrome reports worsening dry mouth after an anticholinergic medication was added for pain. Which step addresses a possible medication-related cause?
o: Increase the dose of the implicated medication to stimulate saliva
Reduce the dose or substitute the medication causing dry mouth
Attribute the worsening symptoms to normal age-related salivary decline
Maintain the dose and set aside the medication as a cause
explanation:
Xerostomia is the sensation of dry mouth. Sjögren syndrome can reduce salivary reserve, so a new drug that blocks muscarinic signaling can worsen dryness. Reviewing its dose or choosing a less anticholinergic analgesic addresses a potentially reversible contributor.

**A. Increase the dose.** Greater anticholinergic exposure can suppress salivation further.
**B. Reduce the dose or substitute the drug.** Lowering the anticholinergic burden may relieve the added dryness while preserving a plan for pain control.
**C. Attribute symptoms to age.** Healthy aging generally preserves daily salivary output. Worsening dryness warrants assessment for disease and medication effects.
**D. Continue the dose and dismiss a drug effect.** Sjögren syndrome and medication-induced dryness can coexist, and the worsening followed the new prescription.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 457–458.

optionRationales.body: . Increase the dose.** Greater anticholinergic exposure can suppress salivation further.
. Reduce the dose or substitute the drug.** Lowering the anticholinergic burden may relieve the added dryness while preserving a plan for pain control.
. Attribute symptoms to age.** Healthy aging generally preserves daily salivary output. Worsening dryness warrants assessment for disease and medication effects.
. Continue the dose and dismiss a drug effect.** Sjögren syndrome and medication-induced dryness can coexist, and the worsening followed the new prescription.

q: An 86-year-old woman has difficulty reaching a distant bathroom at night. After a falls assessment, the team decides to shorten the walking distance needed for toileting. Which aid meets this aim?
o: A raised toilet seat in the bathroom
A shower chair placed in the shower
A transfer bench placed across the bathtub
A bedside commode placed near the bed
explanation:
A functional barrier can be the distance between the bed and the toilet. **A bedside commode shortens the nighttime trip.**

**A. A raised toilet seat in the bathroom** — A raised seat can simplify transfers once she reaches the bathroom.
**B. A shower chair placed in the shower** — A shower chair aids bathing, not night-time access for voiding.
**C. A transfer bench placed across the bathtub** — A tub bench helps cross a bathtub wall, not the distance to a toilet.
**D. A bedside commode placed near the bed** — Place the commode near the bed so she can transfer without walking the length of the room.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch. 47, pp. 704, 708–709.

. A shower chair placed in the shower** — A shower chair aids bathing, not night-time access for voiding.
. A transfer bench placed across the bathtub** — A tub bench helps cross a bathtub wall, not the distance to a toilet.
. A bedside commode placed near the bed** — Place the commode near the bed so she can transfer without walking the length of the room.

q: A 79-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia has completed treatment for aspiration pneumonia but still coughs when drinking. A speech-language pathologist recommends thickened liquids and a pureed diet. Her daughter asks to preserve her usual coffee and food for enjoyment. Which discussion addresses both swallowing risk and the patient’s preferences?
o: Explain thin-liquid aspiration risk and explore diet acceptability and quality of life
Explain that thickened liquids are more easily aspirated and recommend usual coffee
Explain that viscosity does not affect aspiration and use the family’s texture preference
Explain that thin liquids protect the airway and omit discussion of dietary burden
explanation:
Thin drinks can flow into the airway before protection is complete. Thickening can improve the immediate swallow yet reduce enjoyment or willingness to drink. **Discuss aspiration risk alongside what the patient enjoys and how much she will actually eat and drink.**

**A. Explain the risk and explore acceptability** — Involve the patient as far as she can participate, her daughter and the swallowing team. Discuss safe ways to preserve preferred flavors, and monitor intake and hydration.
**B. Thickened drinks are more easily aspirated** — The usual rationale for thickening is to slow flow. Individual response should be assessed.
**C. Viscosity is irrelevant** — Changing viscosity can alter swallowing safety. Family preference alone cannot identify which consistency the patient tolerates.
**D. Thin drinks protect the airway** — Thin coffee can be difficult to control when airway protection is delayed. Its value to this patient belongs in the discussion along with that risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 449–451, adherence, diet modification and patient goals.

. Thickened drinks are more easily aspirated** — The usual rationale for thickening is to slow flow. Individual response should be assessed.
. Viscosity is irrelevant** — Changing viscosity can alter swallowing safety. Family preference alone cannot identify which consistency the patient tolerates.
. Thin drinks protect the airway** — Thin coffee can be difficult to control when airway protection is delayed. Its value to this patient belongs in the discussion along with that risk.

q: An 83-year-old man with CKD and a remote traumatic brain injury from a motorcycle accident at age 25 presents after his first seizure. His wife reports progressive forgetfulness over two years. EEG shows left temporal sharp waves; MRI shows left mesial temporal sclerosis and old right frontal encephalomalacia. His calculated creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. If levetiracetam is selected, which renal prescribing approach follows Table 6 of the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Reduce the levetiracetam dose because impaired kidney function raises concern for central nervous system adverse effects.
Retain the levetiracetam dose because impaired kidney function reduces concern for central nervous system adverse effects.
Increase the levetiracetam dose because impaired kidney function raises concern for inadequate central nervous system exposure.
Avoid levetiracetam treatment because impaired kidney function requires drug avoidance rather than treatment at a reduced dose.
explanation:
Levetiracetam is an antiseizure medicine whose clearance depends on kidney function. Reduced elimination can increase central adverse effects.

**Use a reduced levetiracetam dose at a creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min.** The renal dosing criterion applies at 80 mL/min or lower.

**A. Reduce the dose.** A lower renal-adjusted regimen allows treatment while limiting excess CNS exposure.
**B. Keep the usual dose.** Impaired elimination increases the concern for CNS effects even if the drug is appropriate for the seizure type.
**C. Increase for inadequate exposure.** Low clearance increases exposure to a given dose, so empiric escalation could add harm.
**D. Avoid levetiracetam altogether.** At this clearance, dose adjustment can permit use when the drug is otherwise indicated.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Table 6, p. 2073.

. Keep the usual dose.** Impaired elimination increases the concern for CNS effects even if the drug is appropriate for the seizure type.
. Increase for inadequate exposure.** Low clearance increases exposure to a given dose, so empiric escalation could add harm.
. Avoid levetiracetam altogether.** At this clearance, dose adjustment can permit use when the drug is otherwise indicated.

q: בת 92 עם דמנציה מתקדמת הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. משפחתה מבקשת PEG בגלל שאיפות חוזרות. מה מתואר בסיכום המחקרים במסמך הוועדה הארצית, לצד ההסתייגות ממגבלותיהם?
o: שיעורי השאיפה דומים בין דרכי ההזנה שנבדקו
הזנה ב־PEG מפחיתה שאיפה בהשוואה להזנה פומית
הזנה בזונדה מפחיתה שאיפה בהשוואה להזנה פומית
מתן נוזלים בעירוי מפחית שאיפה בהשוואה להזנה פומית
explanation:
**לא הודגם יתרון עקבי של צינור הזנה במניעת אספירציות** בהשוואות שסקרה הוועדה בדמנציה מתקדמת. גם רוק ותוכן קיבה יכולים להישאף.

**א. שיעורי שאיפה דומים.** כך תוארו ההשוואות, תוך הסתייגות מהטיות ומהבדלים בין אוכלוסיות המחקר.
**ב. PEG מפחית שאיפה.** הוא עוקף חלק ממסלול הבליעה אך אינו מונע כל שאיפה.
**ג. זונדה מפחיתה שאיפה.** הימצאות צינור אינה מבטיחה הגנה על דרכי הנשימה.
**ד. עירוי מפחית שאיפה.** הנתונים אינם מצדיקים המלצה על הזנה תוך־ורידית למניעת אספירציה.

q: An 84-year-old man with symptomatic carotid stenosis is being assessed for intervention. Which comparison between carotid endarterectomy and transfemoral carotid artery stenting is described by Hazzard?
o: More myocardial infarction with endarterectomy and more stroke with transfemoral stenting
More stroke with endarterectomy and more myocardial infarction with transfemoral stenting
Less myocardial infarction with endarterectomy and less stroke with transfemoral stenting
Less cranial nerve injury with endarterectomy and less stroke with transfemoral stenting
explanation:
Carotid endarterectomy removes plaque through a neck incision. Transfemoral stenting traverses the aortic arch and crosses the plaque. **Myocardial infarction is more frequent with endarterectomy, while perioperative stroke is more frequent with transfemoral stenting**, especially at this age.

**A. More infarction with surgery and more stroke with stenting** — The operation adds cardiac stress. Catheter manipulation can dislodge emboli from arch or carotid plaque.
**B. More stroke with surgery and more infarction with stenting** — These comparisons reverse the observed directions of the two procedural risks.
**C. Less infarction with surgery and less stroke with stenting** — Neither advantage applies. The patient's cardiac reserve and embolic risk both matter.
**D. Less cranial nerve injury with surgery and less stroke with stenting** — Surgical dissection near the carotid can injure cranial nerves, often transiently. Older stent recipients have a higher procedural stroke risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1214, carotid interventions and complications.

optionRationales.body: . More infarction with surgery and more stroke with stenting** — The operation adds cardiac stress. Catheter manipulation can dislodge emboli from arch or carotid plaque.
. More stroke with surgery and more infarction with stenting** — These comparisons reverse the observed directions of the two procedural risks.
. Less infarction with surgery and less stroke with stenting** — Neither advantage applies. The patient's cardiac reserve and embolic risk both matter.

. Less cranial nerve injury with surgery and less stroke with stenting** — Surgical dissection near the carotid can injure cranial nerves, often transiently. Older stent recipients have a higher procedural stroke risk.

q: איזו פגיעה בראיה היא גורם הסיכון המשמעותי ביותר לנפילה?
o: ירידה בחדות הראייה (acuity)
ירידה ברגישות לסנוור ( glare )
ירידה בהסתגלות לחושך (adaptation)
ירידה ברגישות לניגודיות ( contrast)
explanation:
A person may read a high-contrast eye chart yet miss the edge of a step against similarly colored pavement. **Reduced contrast sensitivity is the strongest visual predictor among these choices.**

**A. Reduced acuity** — Acuity measures resolution of fine detail. Reduced acuity shows a more modest association with falls than impaired contrast sensitivity.
**B. Change in glare sensitivity** — Glare can impair vision in particular lighting, but it is not the strongly supported measure identified in this comparison.
**C. Reduced dark adaptation** — Difficulty adjusting to dim illumination is distinct from distinguishing an edge against its background.
**D. Reduced contrast sensitivity** — Loss of contrast makes obstacles harder to recognize even in daylight and has a strong association with falls.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 635–636, Table 43-1.

. Change in glare sensitivity** — Glare can impair vision in particular lighting, but it is not the strongly supported measure identified in this comparison.
. Reduced dark adaptation** — Difficulty adjusting to dim illumination is distinct from distinguishing an edge against its background.
. Reduced contrast sensitivity** — Loss of contrast makes obstacles harder to recognize even in daylight and has a strong association with falls.

q: בת 78. ברקע יתר לחץ דם, פרפור עליות, החלפת ברך לפני כ- 3 שנים. פנתה למוקד בשל נפילה עם חבלה בברך. ללא ממצא בבדיקתה הגופנית למעט חבלות יבשות, ללא שברים. בתשאול על מנגנון הנפילה מתארת סחרחרות בעת קימה לשירותים מהמיטה לפנות בוקר. בבדיקתה ערנית ומשתפת פעולה, כאובה ברגל, אך נושאת משקל, סימני שפשוף בברך. דופק לא סדיר 65 לדקה, צבע ונשימה תקינים, ל"ד 135/90 בישיבה, 110/80 בעמידה. מהו הצעד להמשך, בעדיפות ראשונה, על מנת להקטין סיכון לנפילה נוספת?
o: הולטר אק"ג 24 שעות
אקו לב ויעוץ קרדיולוגי
סקירה מחודשת והתאמה של הטיפול התרופתי הקבוע
הפניה לפיזיותרפיה לתרגול מניעת נפילות וחיזוק שרירים
explanation:
The pressure falls by 25 mm Hg systolic and 10 mm Hg diastolic on standing, in keeping with the dizziness on rising. **Review and adjust the regular medications first** to reduce the risk of another orthostatic fall.

**A. Twenty-four-hour Holter** — A short recording may miss infrequent events. The postural trigger and pressure fall already identify a treatable contributor.
**B. Echocardiography and cardiology referral** — Echo can investigate suspected structural disease. No murmur, exertional event or other new cardiac clue is described.
**C. Review the regular regimen** — Identify medicines that reduce pressure or circulating volume. Adjust plausible contributors and reassess standing pressure and symptoms.
**D. Strength and balance training** — Physiotherapy can reduce future falls but cannot directly reverse a drug-related pressure fall.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 667–668, 675.

q: בת 72, סובלת מכאב בכתף שמאל כבר 4 חודשים. הכאב מחמיר בלילה ומפריע לשינה. בבדיקה פיזיקלית נמצאת הגבלה בתנועה אקטיבית ופסיבית כאחד, ללא ממצא חריג בצילום רנטגן, אולטרסאונד ו-MRI. היא אינה זוכרת אירוע טראומטי, אך עברה ניתוח לב לפני כשנה. מה האבחנה הסבירה ביותר?
o: Rotator Cuff Tear
Subacromial Bursitis
Adhesive Capsulitis
Calcific Tendinitis
explanation:
Adhesive capsulitis causes a painful, stiff glenohumeral joint as the capsule thickens and may become fibrotic. **Months of night pain with restriction of both active and passive motion favor adhesive capsulitis.**

**A. Rotator cuff tear** Weakness in external rotation or difficulty controlling adduction suggests a tear. The global passive restriction and normal tendon imaging point elsewhere.
**B. Subacromial bursitis** Elevation typically provokes a painful arc. A global loss of passive movement suggests that the joint capsule itself has stiffened.
**C. Adhesive capsulitis** The examiner cannot restore the lost movement by moving the relaxed arm. Imaging can be unrevealing, and reduced use during recovery from surgery is a possible antecedent.
**D. Calcific tendinitis** Calcium deposits in or around a cuff tendon often appear on radiographs or ultrasound and can cause an acute painful episode.

Reference · Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e, ch. 387, pp. 2974–2975, Adhesive Capsulitis.

q: בן 80, דייר דיור מוגן, ללא ירידה קוגניטיבית, ללא חוק סיעוד, נוהג. ברקע סוכרת מאוזנת תרופתית היטב ואי ספיקת כליות. אובחן עם פרפור עליות חדש. איזה טיפול אנטיקואגולנטי מומלץ בהתאם להנחיות ה- Beers Criteria 2023 update ?
o: עדיפות לטיפול ב- Apixaban במקום Rivaroxaban בגלל פרופיל בטיחות יותר טוב
עדיפות לטיפול ב- Rivaroxaban בעקבות גיל מבוגר ומתן חד יומי
עדיפות לתת Rivaroxaban במידה ו- GFR מתחת ל- 30 מ"ל/לדקה
עדיפות לטיפול ב- Dabigatran בשל אפשרות למתן Antidote במידת הצורך
explanation:
Anticoagulant selection in older adults with AF depends on renal function, adherence and the risk of major bleeding. **Prefer apixaban over rivaroxaban for long-term treatment when both are otherwise suitable**, because apixaban has a more favorable bleeding profile.

**A. Prefer apixaban for safety** — Long-term rivaroxaban has been associated with more major and gastrointestinal bleeding than other direct anticoagulants, particularly apixaban.
**B. Prefer rivaroxaban for age and once-daily dosing** — A once-daily schedule can matter when adherence requires it. Age alone provides no such reason, and this patient's history supplies none.
**C. Prefer rivaroxaban when filtration is below 30** — Renal impairment warrants drug-specific eligibility and dose assessment. It does not make rivaroxaban safer.
**D. Prefer dabigatran because it has an antidote** — Idarucizumab can reverse dabigatran in an emergency. Reversibility alone does not outweigh the bleeding and renal-clearance considerations here.

Reference · 2023 American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria, p. 2058, Table 2, and Tables 4 and 6.

q: גבר בן 79 עם יתר לחץ דם ומחלת כליות כרונית (eGFR= 28) מאושפז בשל סחרחורת וכמעט עילפון. תרופותיו כוללות Lisinopril, Hydrochlorothiazide ו- Clonidine. לפי קריטריוני Beers איזו תרופה סביר ביותר שגורמת לתסמינים ויש להימנע ממנה בטיפול בלחץ דם?
o: Lisinopril
Hydrochlorothiazide
Clonidine
כל התרופות במידה שווה
explanation:
Clonidine suppresses central sympathetic activity and can cause bradycardia, dizziness and orthostatic hypotension. **Review clonidine first in this man with near-syncope**, while checking standing pressure, pulse, volume status, renal function and other drugs. If an established prescription is changed, taper it under supervision to prevent rebound hypertension.

**A. Lisinopril.** It can lower pressure and alter potassium or kidney function, but lacks clonidine's central sympatholytic and bradycardic actions.
**B. Hydrochlorothiazide.** Volume loss or electrolyte abnormalities can also contribute and should be assessed.
**C. Clonidine.** Impaired postural compensation and a slow pulse fit the symptoms. Avoid initiating it as routine first-line hypertension therapy; do not abruptly stop ongoing treatment.
**D. All equally likely.** All lower blood pressure, but the central and postural adverse-effect profile singles out clonidine.

Reference · AGS Beers Criteria 2023, p. 2058. FDA clonidine prescribing information, withdrawal warning.

q: בן 80, נפל ושבר מפרק ירך וזקוק לניתוח. ברקע ידוע על פרפור עליות תחת טיפול ב- APIXABAN (ELIQUIS). מהי ההרדמה המומלצת ומדוע?
o: הרדמה כללית, כי מאפשרת ניתוח מיידי
הרדמה אזורית לאחר יומיים של הפסקת APIXABAN, כי מורידה סיכון לדליריום
הרדמה אזורית לאחר יומיים של הפסקת APIXABAN, כי מפחיתה תמותה
הרדמה כללית כי מפחיתה שימוש באופיואידים לאחר הניתוח
explanation:
Apixaban increases bleeding risk at surgery and around a neuraxial needle. **The dose, time of the last dose, bleeding risk and urgency determine whether a neuraxial technique is appropriate.**

**A. General anesthesia to operate immediately** — It avoids neuraxial puncture and its anticoagulant timing constraints. Surgical bleeding risk still needs assessment before proceeding.
**B. Neuraxial anesthesia after two days to prevent delirium** — Two days is not appropriate for every apixaban dose. In the REGAIN trial, postoperative delirium occurred at similar rates after spinal and general anesthesia.
**C. Neuraxial anesthesia after two days to reduce mortality** — Trials have not shown a survival advantage for spinal anesthesia. ASRA suggests a longer interruption for high-dose apixaban than for low-dose treatment.
**D. General anesthesia to reduce postoperative opioid use** — General anesthesia alone does not ensure less opioid use. A peripheral nerve block and a tailored postoperative analgesic plan address fracture pain.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 797. REGAIN trial, NEJM 2021, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2113514. ASRA fifth edition, apixaban recommendations, doi:10.1136/rapm-2024-105766.
Key note: All four options received credit. Hazzard reports comparable mortality with general and spinal anesthesia and gives no universal two-day apixaban interval.

q: What percentage of patients older than 70 with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis were not offered surgery in the cited European study?
explanation:
Under-referral for valve replacement can leave older adults with symptomatic severe stenosis exposed to the natural history of the disease. The cohorts differed in their age thresholds, so their percentages answer different questions.
**In the European study of patients older than 70, 41% were not offered surgery despite severe symptomatic aortic stenosis.**

**A. 33 percent.** This was the proportion in the separate study of patients older than 75, drawn from 92 centers in 25 countries.
**B. 41 percent.** This refers to the European group older than 70 and measures how often surgery was not offered.
**C. 8.8 percent.** This was overall operative mortality in a Medicare surgical cohort, a different population and outcome.
**D. 6.0 percent.** This was operative mortality at high-volume centers in the Medicare data. It describes the outcome after surgery.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1152, surgical aortic valve replacement.
